prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study is a case report describing how red dichromatic imaging seemed to show a nerve structure better than standard white-light imaging.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patient was a 57-year-old woman who had a minimally invasive endoscopic procedure to remove a small, shallow growth on the pharyngoepiglottic fold.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The nerve appeared sharper and easier to see with the red imaging method than with white light, both before cutting the tissue and after injecting fluid under the surface.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The lesion was removed in one piece, and there were no visible signs of damage to the nerve during the surgery.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patient did not experience difficulty swallowing, a hoarse voice, or any other complications after the operation.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors suggest that this red imaging technique could be a helpful tool for seeing the nerve and supporting efforts to preserve it during similar surgeries.
facts.subject: humans
